Erken İtfa: The repayment of the principal of a debt before its maturity, together with the interest accrued on it.
Esnek ilişki: A one percent increase in one variable resulting in a response of more than one percent in the other variable.
Esnek olmayan ilişki: Or a rigid relationship: a one percent increase in one variable resulting in a response of less than one percent in the other variable.
Esneklik: Or in short ε: the measurement describing by what percentage the variable shown on the vertical axis increases or decreases as a result of a one percent increase in the variable shown on the horizontal axis.
Essential Facilities Doctrine: An asset/facility/infrastructure without which a rival or customer cannot continue its activities by making use of it.
Etki: The social, economic and environmental changes that occur generally within 3-5 years following the completion of a project, positive or negative, expected or unexpected, appearing directly or indirectly.
Etki gecikmesi: The period between the implementation of an economic policy and the effects of that policy being felt.
Etkin Piyasa Hipotezi: This hypothesis predicts that the current prices of instruments traded in a market reflect all the obtainable information relating to those instruments. With the assumption that price is determined by buyers and sellers, the hypothesis assumes that traders can access all attainable information simultaneously and symmetrically. It is predicted that the price formed in this case is the equilibrium price.
Euro Dolar: Used to refer to US dollar deposits held at banks outside the United States or at the foreign branches of US banks. The expression 'Euro' stems from the fact that the great majority of such deposits are held particularly at banks in Western European countries. US dollar accounts held in Asia and all other similar countries are also referred to by this name.
Eurobond: Securities issued by the issuing country or institution in a currency other than its own national currency.
Exclusionary Agreements: Agreements made among undertakings with the aim of preventing or obstructing the activities of rivals.
Exemption: Regulated in Article 13 of the Competition Act. The exemption granted to agreements, concerted practices and decisions of undertaking associations, provided the conditions listed in Article 5 of the Act are satisfied, is not absolute.
Eximbank: In our country, the institution that supports and encourages, by supporting the development of exports, the diversification of exported goods and services, the provision of new markets for exported goods, the increase of exporters' shares in international trade, the provision of the necessary support for exporters' ventures, and the provision of competitive strength and assurance to exporters and to contractors and investors operating abroad in international markets, as well as investments to be made abroad and the production and sale of investment goods aimed at export
Explicit Collusion: The attainment of an explicit understanding among rival undertakings on matters such as the setting of price and production quantity, and the sharing of markets and customers.
Exploitative Practices: Some of the cases evaluated under Article 6 of the Competition Act are characterized as exploitative abuse. These are pricing or other practices causing a direct loss in consumer welfare. In such abuses, the dominant undertaking uses the advantage of its market power with the aim of extracting rent from consumers in a way a non-dominant undertaking could not. Excessive pricing and applying unfair trading conditions are among these cases.
Export Cartel: Undertakings operating in the same country acting together to sell or market their products in external markets, thereby obtaining an advantage against their international rivals. This can emerge in forms such as export prices being set jointly by rival undertakings, the sharing of customers, decisions on whether products are to be sold to certain regions via patent or license — that is, the conduct of an export restricted relative to what would occur in a free trade environment
Externalities: Externality refers to the situations in which the production or consumption of goods and services brings a cost (negative externality) or a benefit (positive externality) to other persons. Externalities, which are one of the market failures and create inefficiency, may not be reflected in the prices of the goods and services offered. Pollution is a clear example of a negative externality, also called external diseconomy. Chemical wastes dumped into a lake by an industrial facility, killing the fish and plants in the lake,
Eğim: Or in short μ: the measurement describing by how many units the variable shown on the vertical axis increases or decreases as a result of a one-unit increase in the variable shown on the horizontal axis.
Eğitimi Programı: The training program that those wishing to benefit from the supports KOSGEB offers to entrepreneurs who want to establish their own business are required to attend beforehand.
Eş Finansman: The cash contribution committed to being provided by the grant beneficiary, to be spent in the supported project or activity.
Eşmaliyet doğrusu: A graphical tool showing the combinations of production factors that can be purchased with the same fixed expenditure.
Eşürün eğrisi: A graphical tool showing the input combinations yielding the same total product, all else being constant.
Eşürün haritası: The whole of the multiple isoquant curves showing different total product quantities.
Faaliyet kârı: The situation in which the revenue obtained from production can fully cover the variable expenses arising from production.
Faaliyet zararı: The situation in which the revenue obtained from production cannot fully cover the variable expenses arising from production.
Failing Firm: The firm that is continuously loss-making, to the point where the liquidation of its business becomes likely, and is losing market share.
Failing Firm Defense: Mergers and acquisitions resulting in a substantial restriction of competition can, in some special cases, be permitted on the basis of economic and rational justifications; the failing firm defense constitutes one of these special cases.
Faiz: The predetermined payment made in return for using capital belonging to someone else.
Faiz dışı bütçe dengesi: The budget balance calculated with the state's interest payments excluded.
Faiz riski: The risk of an unexpected change in the interest rate adversely affecting the value of debts and receivables.
Faizsiz Kredi Desteği: The financial support envisaging that the entirety of the interest or profit-share expenses to be paid in return for the credits to be received from the relevant intermediary institutions is covered by the relevant public institutions and organizations.
Faktoring: The transaction in which firms engaged in the sale of goods and services for domestic and foreign markets obtain liquid funds in return for transferring the short-term commercial receivable rights that have arisen or will arise from the sale of goods and services. Besides this, the financial institutions providing firms with the opportunity to collect the proceeds of credit sales before their maturity are also called 'factoring' institutions. These firms purchase the invoiced receivables of companies that have made credit sales in cash but at a discount, and collect the receivable themselves when it matures.
Faktör maliyeti: Or input cost: the cost of the inputs such as labor, capital and land used in the production process.
Faktör piyasası: Or the input market: the markets where the instruments and materials required for production are bought and sold.
FAVÖK: Earnings before interest, taxes and depreciation (EBITDA); it shows business performance independent of financing and depreciation policy.
Fayda: Or in short U: the conceptual measure showing the satisfaction and benefits a consumer derives from a certain good or service.
Fayda fonksiyonu: The mathematical relationship showing how total utility changes depending on the quantity consumed.
Fayda kuramı: The body of principles explaining what products a consumer wishing to raise material living quality will consume or can obtain, and in what quantities.
Fayda maksimizasyonu: The selection of the product bundle that will maximize total utility using a certain budget, with product prices given.
Faydalı Model: An industrial property right granting the owners of inventions applicable in industry the right to produce and market the product.
Fazlalık: Or excess supply: the situation in which the quantity supplied in the market exceeds the quantity demanded.
Federal Fon Oranları: The money market interest rate at which financial institutions in the United States carry out their overnight borrowing. Since it is of the nature of a fundamental indicator in the implementation of monetary policy, it is under the close supervision of the US central bank (FED). With the aim of the daily 'Federal Funds Rates' forming in this market following a course consistent with its announced target rate, the FED adjusts the daily reserve (available funds) amount in the market through open market operations. For example, if the interest rates forming in this market are below the FED's target rate — in other words, if there is a fund surplus in the market — the FED withdraws this amount from the market through open market operations.
Federal Fon Oranı: The interest rate applied to the transaction in which banks and other depositary institutions in the United States lend their free reserves in their Fed accounts overnight.
Fiat para: General payment instruments that have no significant concrete use value and gain value and function through laws and state guarantee.
Finans hesabı: The main heading in the balance of payments showing the changes relating to financial assets and liabilities.
Finans Hesabı - Ödemeler Dengesi Tanımlı: An account in which the short- and long-term international capital flows carried out by the central bank, general government (central administration, local administrations, social security funds), banks and other sectors (other financial corporations and non-financial corporations, households and non-profit institutions) are recorded; it fundamentally contains the changes in a country's external financial assets and liabilities and the counterpart records of these changes.
Finansal bağımsızlık: The central bank's having sufficient financial resources to fulfill its targets and being able to determine its own budget.
Finansal Bulaşıcılık/Yayılma: International investors who are alarmed by problems arising in one or a few countries rapidly withdrawing their investments from countries with similar characteristics, whereby the adverse investment conditions spread also to the financial systems of other countries.
Finansal Derinleşme: The growth of financial services enabling wider service options to reach every segment of society. It can also be defined as the ratio at which the funds created in the financial sector are transferred to the real sector. The term 'financial deepening' can be used in a different sense in relation to the macro effects it brings to economies. Accordingly, greater financial deepening means an increase in the money supply, and the increase in the money supply brings economic growth along with it.
Finansal Eğitim: The process in which, through individuals being informed on financial matters, awareness of financial products, opportunities and risks increases, and consumers and investors, learning the ways of accessing financial information, develop the ability to reflect the knowledge and competence they acquire onto their economic behavior and to make conscious financial decisions.
